sources.title: Google SRE Book — Designing Distributed Systems

functionalRequirements: Core user journeys for URL Shortener are available with stable identifiers
Support authenticated access with audit trails for URL Shortener mutations
Expose paginated list APIs and idempotent write endpoints
nonFunctionalRequirements: 99.9% availability (interview assumption)
p95 read latency < 300ms at 500 QPS average
Writes remain correct under client retries
requirementDistractors: Must be strongly consistent globally with zero latency
Must never use caching
boss.estimationScenario: Design URL Shortener: 40M DAU, 6 actions/day each, read:write = 4:1, peak factor 6×. Estimate hot-path QPS and 2.0 TB/year media/metadata growth.
boss.apiPrompt: Draft REST/JSON APIs for URL Shortener including auth, idempotency keys, cursor pagination, and error codes for rate limits.
deepDivePrompts: How do you shard the hottest entities in URL Shortener?
Which failure scenarios (AZ loss, broker lag, cache stampede) do you mitigate first?
How do you observe p95 and error budget burn for this service?
boss.tradeoffPrompt: Justify SQL vs NoSQL (or cache vs source-of-truth) for URL Shortener metadata.

minSeparation.reason: Keep credentials and invariants off the public internet

boss.referenceNotes: Reference URL Shortener architecture: sync path through gateway + cache, async side effects via queue. Failure scenarios: primary DB failover, queue backlog, cache cold start—state mitigations.
boss.workedEstimate: 40M DAU × 6 actions = 240M ops/day ≈ 2.8k QPS avg; 6× peak ≈ 5000 QPS. Metadata/media growth ≈ 2.0 TB/year before compaction.
deepDiveAnswers: Hash-partition by user_id; isolate celebrity/hot keys to dedicated shards.
Use cache aside with TTL+jitter; protect DB with circuit breakers and request coalescing.
AZ loss: multi-AZ replicas, rehearsed failover, queue redrive policies.
boss.tradeoffAnalysis: Prefer OLTP SQL when invariants matter; add read models/cache for fan-out. Document consistency window for async consumers.
alternativeArchitectures: Event-sourced core with materialized views
CQRS read pools fed by CDC

boss.estimationScenario: Design Unique ID Generator: 40M DAU, 6 actions/day each, read:write = 4:1, peak factor 6×. Estimate hot-path QPS and 0.8 TB/year media/metadata growth.
boss.apiPrompt: Draft REST/JSON APIs for Unique ID Generator including auth, idempotency keys, cursor pagination, and error codes for rate limits.
deepDivePrompts: How do you shard the hottest entities in Unique ID Generator?

minSeparation.reason: Keep credentials and invariants off the public internet

boss.referenceNotes: Reference Unique ID Generator architecture: sync path through gateway + cache, async side effects via queue. Failure scenarios: primary DB failover, queue backlog, cache cold start—state mitigations.
boss.workedEstimate: 40M DAU × 6 actions = 240M ops/day ≈ 2.8k QPS avg; 6× peak ≈ 5411 QPS. Metadata/media growth ≈ 0.8 TB/year before compaction.
deepDiveAnswers: Hash-partition by user_id; isolate celebrity/hot keys to dedicated shards.
Use cache aside with TTL+jitter; protect DB with circuit breakers and request coalescing.
AZ loss: multi-AZ replicas, rehearsed failover, queue redrive policies.
boss.tradeoffAnalysis: Prefer OLTP SQL when invariants matter; add read models/cache for fan-out. Document consistency window for async consumers.
alternativeArchitectures: Event-sourced core with materialized views
CQRS read pools fed by CDC

functionalRequirements: Core user journeys for Notification System are available with stable identifiers
Support authenticated access with audit trails for Notification System mutations
Expose paginated list APIs and idempotent write endpoints
nonFunctionalRequirements: 99.9% availability (interview assumption)
p95 read latency < 300ms at 582 QPS average
Writes remain correct under client retries
requirementDistractors: Must be strongly consistent globally with zero latency
Must never use caching
boss.estimationScenario: Design Notification System: 40M DAU, 6 actions/day each, read:write = 4:1, peak factor 6×. Estimate hot-path QPS and 1.7 TB/year media/metadata growth.
boss.apiPrompt: Draft REST/JSON APIs for Notification System including auth, idempotency keys, cursor pagination, and error codes for rate limits.
deepDivePrompts: How do you shard the hottest entities in Notification System?
Which failure scenarios (AZ loss, broker lag, cache stampede) do you mitigate first?
How do you observe p95 and error budget burn for this service?
boss.tradeoffPrompt: Justify SQL vs NoSQL (or cache vs source-of-truth) for Notification System metadata.

minSeparation.reason: Keep credentials and invariants off the public internet

boss.referenceNotes: Reference Notification System architecture: sync path through gateway + cache, async side effects via queue. Failure scenarios: primary DB failover, queue backlog, cache cold start—state mitigations.
boss.workedEstimate: 40M DAU × 6 actions = 240M ops/day ≈ 2.8k QPS avg; 6× peak ≈ 5822 QPS. Metadata/media growth ≈ 1.7 TB/year before compaction.
deepDiveAnswers: Hash-partition by user_id; isolate celebrity/hot keys to dedicated shards.
Use cache aside with TTL+jitter; protect DB with circuit breakers and request coalescing.
AZ loss: multi-AZ replicas, rehearsed failover, queue redrive policies.
boss.tradeoffAnalysis: Prefer OLTP SQL when invariants matter; add read models/cache for fan-out. Document consistency window for async consumers.
alternativeArchitectures: Event-sourced core with materialized views
CQRS read pools fed by CDC

functionalRequirements: Core user journeys for WhatsApp are available with stable identifiers

nonFunctionalRequirements: 99.9% availability (interview assumption)

boss.estimationScenario: Design WhatsApp: 40M DAU, 6 actions/day each, read:write = 4:1, peak factor 6×. Estimate hot-path QPS and 0.5 TB/year media/metadata growth.
boss.apiPrompt: Draft REST/JSON APIs for WhatsApp including auth, idempotency keys, cursor pagination, and error codes for rate limits.
deepDivePrompts: How do you shard the hottest entities in WhatsApp?

boss.tradeoffPrompt: Justify SQL vs NoSQL (or cache vs source-of-truth) for WhatsApp metadata.

minSeparation.reason: Keep credentials and invariants off the public internet

boss.referenceNotes: Reference WhatsApp architecture: sync path through gateway + cache, async side effects via queue. Failure scenarios: primary DB failover, queue backlog, cache cold start—state mitigations.
boss.workedEstimate: 40M DAU × 6 actions = 240M ops/day ≈ 2.8k QPS avg; 6× peak ≈ 6233 QPS. Metadata/media growth ≈ 0.5 TB/year before compaction.
deepDiveAnswers: Hash-partition by user_id; isolate celebrity/hot keys to dedicated shards.
Use cache aside with TTL+jitter; protect DB with circuit breakers and request coalescing.
AZ loss: multi-AZ replicas, rehearsed failover, queue redrive policies.
boss.tradeoffAnalysis: Prefer OLTP SQL when invariants matter; add read models/cache for fan-out. Document consistency window for async consumers.
alternativeArchitectures: Event-sourced core with materialized views
CQRS read pools fed by CDC

functionalRequirements: Core user journeys for Netflix are available with stable identifiers
Support authenticated access with audit trails for Netflix mutations
Expose paginated list APIs and idempotent write endpoints
nonFunctionalRequirements: 99.9% availability (interview assumption)
p95 read latency < 300ms at 664 QPS average
Writes remain correct under client retries
requirementDistractors: Must be strongly consistent globally with zero latency
Must never use caching
boss.estimationScenario: Design Netflix: 40M DAU, 6 actions/day each, read:write = 4:1, peak factor 6×. Estimate hot-path QPS and 1.4 TB/year media/metadata growth.
boss.apiPrompt: Draft REST/JSON APIs for Netflix including auth, idempotency keys, cursor pagination, and error codes for rate limits.
deepDivePrompts: How do you shard the hottest entities in Netflix?
Which failure scenarios (AZ loss, broker lag, cache stampede) do you mitigate first?
How do you observe p95 and error budget burn for this service?
boss.tradeoffPrompt: Justify SQL vs NoSQL (or cache vs source-of-truth) for Netflix metadata.

minSeparation.reason: Keep credentials and invariants off the public internet

boss.referenceNotes: Reference Netflix architecture: sync path through gateway + cache, async side effects via queue. Failure scenarios: primary DB failover, queue backlog, cache cold start—state mitigations.
boss.workedEstimate: 40M DAU × 6 actions = 240M ops/day ≈ 2.8k QPS avg; 6× peak ≈ 6644 QPS. Metadata/media growth ≈ 1.4 TB/year before compaction.
deepDiveAnswers: Hash-partition by user_id; isolate celebrity/hot keys to dedicated shards.
Use cache aside with TTL+jitter; protect DB with circuit breakers and request coalescing.
AZ loss: multi-AZ replicas, rehearsed failover, queue redrive policies.
boss.tradeoffAnalysis: Prefer OLTP SQL when invariants matter; add read models/cache for fan-out. Document consistency window for async consumers.
alternativeArchitectures: Event-sourced core with materialized views
CQRS read pools fed by CDC

sources.title: Google SRE Book — Designing Distributed Systems

functionalRequirements: Core user journeys for Google Docs are available with stable identifiers
Support authenticated access with audit trails for Google Docs mutations
Expose paginated list APIs and idempotent write endpoints
nonFunctionalRequirements: 99.9% availability (interview assumption)
p95 read latency < 300ms at 705 QPS average
Writes remain correct under client retries
requirementDistractors: Must be strongly consistent globally with zero latency
Must never use caching
boss.estimationScenario: Design Google Docs: 40M DAU, 6 actions/day each, read:write = 4:1, peak factor 6×. Estimate hot-path QPS and 2.3 TB/year media/metadata growth.
boss.apiPrompt: Draft REST/JSON APIs for Google Docs including auth, idempotency keys, cursor pagination, and error codes for rate limits.
deepDivePrompts: How do you shard the hottest entities in Google Docs?
Which failure scenarios (AZ loss, broker lag, cache stampede) do you mitigate first?
How do you observe p95 and error budget burn for this service?
boss.tradeoffPrompt: Justify SQL vs NoSQL (or cache vs source-of-truth) for Google Docs metadata.

minSeparation.reason: Keep credentials and invariants off the public internet

boss.referenceNotes: Reference Google Docs architecture: sync path through gateway + cache, async side effects via queue. Failure scenarios: primary DB failover, queue backlog, cache cold start—state mitigations.
boss.workedEstimate: 40M DAU × 6 actions = 240M ops/day ≈ 2.8k QPS avg; 6× peak ≈ 7055 QPS. Metadata/media growth ≈ 2.3 TB/year before compaction.
deepDiveAnswers: Hash-partition by user_id; isolate celebrity/hot keys to dedicated shards.
Use cache aside with TTL+jitter; protect DB with circuit breakers and request coalescing.
AZ loss: multi-AZ replicas, rehearsed failover, queue redrive policies.
boss.tradeoffAnalysis: Prefer OLTP SQL when invariants matter; add read models/cache for fan-out. Document consistency window for async consumers.
alternativeArchitectures: Event-sourced core with materialized views
CQRS read pools fed by CDC

deepDiveAnswers: Hash-partition by user_id; isolate celebrity/hot keys to dedicated shards.

boss.tradeoffAnalysis: Prefer OLTP SQL when invariants matter; add read models/cache for fan-out. Document consistency window for async consumers.
alternativeArchitectures: Event-sourced core with materialized views

boss.estimationScenario: Design Hotstar IPL Live Streaming: 40M DAU, 6 actions/day each, read:write = 4:1, peak factor 6×. Estimate hot-path QPS and 2.0 TB/year media/metadata growth.
boss.apiPrompt: Draft REST/JSON APIs for Hotstar IPL Live Streaming including auth, idempotency keys, cursor pagination, and error codes for rate limits.
deepDivePrompts: How do you shard the hottest entities in Hotstar IPL Live Streaming?

boss.tradeoffPrompt: Justify SQL vs NoSQL (or cache vs source-of-truth) for Hotstar IPL Live Streaming metadata.

minSeparation.reason: Keep credentials and invariants off the public internet

boss.referenceNotes: Reference Hotstar IPL Live Streaming architecture: sync path through gateway + cache, async side effects via queue. Failure scenarios: primary DB failover, queue backlog, cache cold start—state mitigations.
boss.workedEstimate: 40M DAU × 6 actions = 240M ops/day ≈ 2.8k QPS avg; 6× peak ≈ 9795 QPS. Metadata/media growth ≈ 2.0 TB/year before compaction.
deepDiveAnswers: Hash-partition by user_id; isolate celebrity/hot keys to dedicated shards.
Use cache aside with TTL+jitter; protect DB with circuit breakers and request coalescing.
AZ loss: multi-AZ replicas, rehearsed failover, queue redrive policies.
boss.tradeoffAnalysis: Prefer OLTP SQL when invariants matter; add read models/cache for fan-out. Document consistency window for async consumers.
alternativeArchitectures: Event-sourced core with materialized views
CQRS read pools fed by CDC

sources.title: Google SRE Book — Designing Distributed Systems

functionalRequirements: Core user journeys for S3-like Object Storage are available with stable identifiers
Support authenticated access with audit trails for S3-like Object Storage mutations
Expose paginated list APIs and idempotent write endpoints
nonFunctionalRequirements: 99.9% availability (interview assumption)
p95 read latency < 300ms at 1020 QPS average
Writes remain correct under client retries
requirementDistractors: Must be strongly consistent globally with zero latency
Must never use caching
boss.estimationScenario: Design S3-like Object Storage: 40M DAU, 6 actions/day each, read:write = 4:1, peak factor 6×. Estimate hot-path QPS and 0.8 TB/year media/metadata growth.
boss.apiPrompt: Draft REST/JSON APIs for S3-like Object Storage including auth, idempotency keys, cursor pagination, and error codes for rate limits.
deepDivePrompts: How do you shard the hottest entities in S3-like Object Storage?
Which failure scenarios (AZ loss, broker lag, cache stampede) do you mitigate first?
How do you observe p95 and error budget burn for this service?
boss.tradeoffPrompt: Justify SQL vs NoSQL (or cache vs source-of-truth) for S3-like Object Storage metadata.

minSeparation.reason: Keep credentials and invariants off the public internet

boss.referenceNotes: Reference S3-like Object Storage architecture: sync path through gateway + cache, async side effects via queue. Failure scenarios: primary DB failover, queue backlog, cache cold start—state mitigations.
boss.workedEstimate: 40M DAU × 6 actions = 240M ops/day ≈ 2.8k QPS avg; 6× peak ≈ 10206 QPS. Metadata/media growth ≈ 0.8 TB/year before compaction.
deepDiveAnswers: Hash-partition by user_id; isolate celebrity/hot keys to dedicated shards.
Use cache aside with TTL+jitter; protect DB with circuit breakers and request coalescing.
AZ loss: multi-AZ replicas, rehearsed failover, queue redrive policies.
boss.tradeoffAnalysis: Prefer OLTP SQL when invariants matter; add read models/cache for fan-out. Document consistency window for async consumers.
alternativeArchitectures: Event-sourced core with materialized views
CQRS read pools fed by CDC
